chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the price of fresh juice before it ferments, for the one who buys it to cook with it or to make it into wine. He said: 'If you sell it before it becomes wine, it is permissible, and there is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell fresh juice before it ferments into wine?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in sales by distinguishing between the intrinsic state of the commodity and the buyer's future intent. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that selling juice before fermentation is valid because the substance itself is pure (*halal*) at the time of transaction, regardless of whether the buyer converts it to wine, thereby separating the ruling of the sale from the ruling of the consumption. This highlights the Shia juristic view that the permissibility of a contract depends on the attributes of the item at the moment of exchange.
